steps.title: Prepare lipid film
steps.instruction: Mix the desired lipids (dissolved in chloroform) in a glass vial, dry the mixture under a stream of argon, then desiccate under vacuum for 1 hour to obtain a dry lipid film.

substeps.instruction: Add lipids dissolved in chloroform to a glass vial according to the composition specified in the figure legends.
Dry the mixture under a stream of argon.
Place the vial under vacuum for 01:00:00 to form a dry lipid film.

steps.title: Rehydrate lipid film with buffer
steps.instruction: Rehydrate the dry lipid film with the appropriate buffer (SEC300 or SEC150) depending on the downstream assay, using the buffer compositions listed below.

substeps.instruction: For tethering or lipid‑transfer assays, use SEC300 buffer: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 300 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP.
For ATG9A proteoliposome reconstitution, use SEC150 buffer: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT.

steps.title: Sonicate lipid suspension
steps.instruction: Gently mix the rehydrated lipid suspension and sonicate in a bath sonicator for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Extrude through 0.1 µm membrane
steps.instruction: Pass the sonicated lipid mixture through a 0.1 µm Whatman membrane (Cat# 10419504) using an Avanti Mini‑Extruder (Cat# 610024).

steps.title: Set final lipid concentration
steps.instruction: Adjust the final lipid concentration to 1 mg mL⁻¹ for standard small‑unilamellar vesicles (SUVs) or 0.5 mg mL⁻¹ in the final suspension as required.

steps.title: Add CHAPS to SUV suspension
steps.instruction: Adjust the SUV suspension to a final concentration of 2 % CHAPS (Glycon, Cat# D99009‑25G).

steps.title: Solubilize SUVs with CHAPS
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL of liposomes with 26 µL of 10 % CHAPS (to reach 2 % CHAPS final) and add 4 µL of buffer; incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

substeps.instruction: Combine 100 µL liposomes, 26 µL 10 % CHAPS, and 4 µL buffer.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 01:00:00.

steps.title: Incorporate purified ATG9A‑GFP
steps.instruction: Add purified ATG9A‑GFP (in 0.2 % DDM) to the CHAPS‑solubilized SUVs at a 1:1 volume ratio to achieve a final ATG9A‑GFP concentration of 0.5 µM.

steps.title: Add 6xHis‑ATG9A‑GFP to SUVs
steps.instruction: Add 65 µL of 6xHis‑ATG9A‑GFP (~1 µM) to 65 µL of the CHAPS‑solubilized SUVs (or 65 µL buffer for mock samples) and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 65 µL of 6xHis‑ATG9A‑GFP (~1 µM) into the CHAPS‑solubilized SUV mixture (or buffer only for controls).

steps.title: Dilute to reduce detergent levels
steps.instruction: Dilute the mixture with SEC150 buffer to lower detergent concentrations to approximately 0.003 % DDM and 0.07 % CHAPS.

steps.title: Overnight dialysis with Bio‑Beads
steps.instruction: Dialyze the diluted mixture overnight at 4 °C against SEC150 buffer containing 0.1 g L⁻¹ Bio‑Beads SM‑2 (Bio‑Rad, Cat# 1523920).

steps.title: Incubate with fresh Bio‑Beads
steps.instruction: Incubate the dialyzed mixture for 1 hour at room temperature with fresh Bio‑Beads.

steps.title: Low‑speed centrifugation to remove beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample in a benchtop centrifuge at low speed for 1 minute to pellet and remove Bio‑Beads.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation to clear aggregates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant at maximum speed in a benchtop centrifuge for 30 minutes to pellet any aggregates.

steps.title: Collect proteoliposome supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the final supernatant, which contains the ATG9A proteoliposomes, for use in downstream assays.
